---
title: "WF4 — Simulate system"
---

`simulate_system.smk` runs Wflow-SBM for explicit series in a ready WF3 collection and reduces retained native responses to named indicator sets. Invoke it through `scripts/simulate_system.py`, which validates the selected operations and indicator sets before Snakemake starts.

## Rules

| Rule | Operation |
|---|---|
| `all` (target) | Collect the selected metric set and records. |
| 4.01 `write_model_fingerprint` | Record the model reference. |
| 4.02 `check_model_unchanged` | Verify the live model against its reference. |
| 4.03 `snapshot_simulation_inputs` | Freeze collection, model, settings, and environment identity. |
| 4.04 `downscale_scenario_series` | Prepare per-run model forcing. |
| 4.05 `run_wflow_simulations_batch_<batch>` | Run Wflow in batches, retaining native responses. |
| 4.06 `publish_wflow_outputs` | Publish the response inventory. |
| `simulations_only` (target) | Collect simulation outputs without indicators. |
| 4.07 `prepare_indicator_plan` | Resolve each distinct metric request's identity and targets. |
| 4.08 `derive_system_indicators` | Produce each immutable metric set: tables, coverage evidence and marker. |
| 4.09 `gather_logs` | Merge experiment logs. |
| 4.10 `gather_benchmarks` | Merge experiment benchmarks. |
| `simulations_and_indicators` (target) | Collect the selected metric set. |

The runner infers its target from `operations`: both operations run `all`, simulations alone stop at `simulations_only`, and indicators alone read completed responses without rerunning Wflow. Sets with identical numerical requests share one plan and one immutable metric set. After Snakemake, the runner publishes each set separately; a failed set keeps its previous publication, and the command exits nonzero unless every set is current. With several sets, Snakemake runs with `--keep-going`, which also lets independent Wflow batches continue after one fails.

## Rule flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["4.01–4.03 Verify model and freeze inputs"] --> B["4.04 Downscale series"]
  B --> C["4.05 Run Wflow batches"]
  C --> D["4.06 Publish responses"]
  D --> E["4.07 Plan indicators"]
  E --> F["4.08 Derive metric set"]
  D --> G["simulations_only target"]
  F --> H["simulations_and_indicators target"]
  D --> I["4.09–4.10 Records"]
  F --> I
```

Indicators alone start from existing retained responses and proceed through the indicator branch. Simulations alone stop after response publication.

## Configuration

The project file supplies the `model` context and `workflows.simulate_system.enabled` and `.config_path`; the latter resolves the workflow YAML beside the project file. The WF4 file, `test_case/project_config_rapid_simulate_system.yml`, sets `experiment_name` (the output namespace), `operations` and `indicator_sets`. The template at `config/templates/project_config.simulate_system.template.yml` also describes the optional `compute` block: `julia_threads`, `max_parallel_batches`, `batch_size_max`, `batch_size`, and `disk_headroom_gb`.

```yaml
experiment_name: experiment_rapid
operations: [simulations, indicators]   # either alone; omitted means both
indicator_sets: [default, example_subset]
indicator_set_definitions:
  example_subset:
    config_path: indicator_sets/example_subset.yml   # relative to this file
```

`operations` is a nonempty list of unique entries from `simulations` and `indicators`; order does not matter. `indicator_sets` lists set ids (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, at most 64 characters); omitted means `[default]`. `default` is bundled at `config/indicator_sets/default.yml` and expands to the existing suite for `model.outvars` (the toolbox defaults when the key is absent, or the retained variables when indicators run alone). A custom set's `config_path` may be absolute; a relative path resolves against the WF4 file that declares it. Selected set files are read once per invocation. Copy `config/templates/indicator_set.template.yml` for a custom set: it selects registered definitions, or names one registered calculation under an authored id. A set never defines arithmetic, units, calendars, missingness or grain.

Selected indicators must be available: before simulating, their variables are checked against `model.outvars`; when indicators run alone, against the retained responses. A missing variable fails with the set, metric, method and variable; it never schedules a simulation.

The scalar `operation: simulate-and-metrics | metrics-only` and `metrics:` token list remain accepted for one feature release as the legacy interface, with their explicit `--target` rules. They cannot be mixed with `operations`/`indicator_sets`; see `dev/records/milestones/post-r12/migration_named-indicator-sets.md`.

## Inputs

WF4 can run with WF3 disabled when its selected collection is already ready. For a project-generation
selection, the runner binds any pending experiment seed from the validated existing generation plan
together with the collection. It preserves an already-bound seed and does not regenerate scenarios.

WF4 requires the completed WF1 model and an explicitly selected ready WF3 collection and run IDs. It checks the model reference and freezes the selected collection, model, settings, and environment identity for the experiment. It does not consume WF2 projections.

## Outputs

An experiment retains native Wflow response CSVs and a response inventory. Each immutable metric set (`metric-set/4`, under the experiment's `_engine/metric_sets/<id>/`) retains `metrics.json`, its indicator tables, group membership, declarations, return-level evidence and per-series block coverage. Each selected set is published as a readable view at `results/metric_sets/<set-id>/`: run and group tables, group lookups and an `indicators.csv` dictionary of units, methods, temporal and missingness policies, and coverage. Logs and benchmarks are scoped to the experiment. See [Reading the outputs](../guide/outputs.qmd) for paths and join keys.
